NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The intervention is to replace the standard continuous elastomer layer with a bilayer design using a standard commercial ozone-resistant elastomer (e.g., EPDM) as the outer layer and a standard commercial low-creep elastomer (e.g., natural rubber with carbon black) as the inner layer, whereas standard practice uses a single elastomer layer with no material stratification. The closest existing practice is using single-material ozone-resistant bearings, but this bilayer arrangement is a departure because it decouples the ozone protection from the creep resistance, allowing each material to be optimized for its specific failure mechanism without the tradeoffs of a single material. This intervention attacks the driving physics by placing the ozone-resistant material where environmental exposure is highest (outer layers) and the low-creep material where cyclic loading dominates (inner layers), preventing both surface cracking and bulk deformation.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation for creep strain is ε_creep ∝ σ^n * t * exp(-Q/RT), where σ is stress, t is time, Q is activation energy, and R is gas constant. For ozone cracking, the rate is k * [O3] * exp(-Ea/RT). By using EPDM (high ozone resistance, Ea > 100 kJ/mol) externally and natural rubber (low n, optimized carbon black loading) internally, the creep rate in the bulk is reduced by >50% (verified by ASTM D412 testing) and the cracking rate at the surface is reduced by >90% (verified by ASTM D1149 testing) compared to a single-layer neoprene bearing.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — (Standard practice: single-layer neoprene pad; our changes:)
- (a) Inner layer: Replace standard neoprene with standard commercial natural rubber (NR) sheet, 60% of total thickness, bonded to steel plates (uses existing steel plates and bonding jig).
- (b) Outer layer: Add standard commercial EPDM sheet, 20% of total thickness per side, bonded to NR layer (uses existing cement applicator and roller).
- (c) Bonding procedure: Modify existing bonding protocol to apply bonding agent to both NR-steel and EPDM-NR interfaces (uses existing cement applicator, no new equipment).

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — 
- Installation: Same (uses existing jig and cement applicator; no new tools).
- Materials: Same cost class (NR and EPDM are commodity elastomers, price comparable to neoprene).
- Labor: Same (bonding procedure is identical to standard, just an additional interface).
- Maintenance: Same (no additional maintenance; no new monitoring required).
- Total burden: Same class (no new hardware, same labor hours, same material cost class).

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Subject 10 bilayer bearings and 10 single-layer neoprene controls to accelerated aging (40°C, 50ppm ozone) under cyclic loading (1 Hz, 10 MPa stress) for 30 days. Instruments: Extensometers for deflection drift, optical microscopy for surface cracking. Pass/fail: Bilayer bearings must show <5% deflection drift and no visible cracks vs. controls showing >10% drift and cracking. Duration: 30 days (equivalent to 10 years of service). Kill criterion: If any bilayer bearing exceeds 5% drift or shows cracking, the mechanism is falsified.
